newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Hainan Airlines aims to list by year-end.
newsitem.headline: China's Hainan Airlines aims to list by year-end.

text.p: Hainan Airlines aims to list 71 million foreign currency B shares on the Shanghai market by the end of 1996, a company official said on Friday.
An issue price has yet to be fixed and the company has selected China's J and A Securities as its lead underwriter, she said by telephone from the Hainan provincial capital of Haikou.
The company will be the first Chinese airline to issue B shares.
The firm has received regulatory approval for the issue, the China Securities newspaper said on Friday.
The company is 25 percent owned by American Aviation Investment, a fund partially controlled by U.S. financier George Soros, making it the first Chinese airline to become a joint venture company.
The firm will use proceeds from the issue to acquire new planes and related equipment, the official said.
"The investor response will be very good," she said. "The aviation business in China is developing quickly and has an excellent future."
The firm operates more than 30 domestic routes and aims to start overseas routes in 1997, she said.
It posted turnover of 480 million yuan in 1995, she said but declined to give a forecast for 1996.
In August, a company official said 1995 net earnings were 81 million yuan, down from 87 million in 1994.
